officialReleaseNotes: Build 254: original English-to-Italian Exercise Laboratory covering every current authoring preset and its supported modes.
title: QQL Demo: Exercise Laboratory
courseDescription: An English-to-Italian laboratory for trying every current Exercise type and its meaningful authoring options. Five Lessons group Select, Input, Arrange, Match and Presentation; a sixth Lesson is a Story, a seventh holds Assign (Sort into groups, Fill the slots) and an eighth shows Pages. Inspect or Fork the Course in Course Studio to study how the exercises are authored. Enable Audio Exercises and Text-to-speech to include all listening and pronunciation examples; ordinary lesson progression remains in effect.

content.text: Choose an answer, select a complete set, or fill fixed gaps with reusable options. The Rounds also demonstrate images, characters, reading, dialogue, listening and both translation directions. Listening needs Enable Audio Exercises and Text-to-speech in Audio Settings; Preview ignores those learner switches.

prompt.text: Read the instruction carefully. Single-answer questions check immediately. Multiple-answer questions wait for Check; select every correct option and no distractor.
How do you say ‘thank you’ in Italian?
How do you say ‘the apple’ in Italian?
Which words are Italian colours? Select all correct answers.
Which words name an animal? Select all correct answers.
Which word means ‘yes’? Select the correct answer, then press Check.

rounds.title: One missing word, one word for all gaps

prompt.text: In Pick the missing word, choose the one missing expression. In One word fills all, one word fits every gap: choose it once and it appears in each gap.
Anna ___ un caffè. Luca ___ un tè.
Match words to pictures, then inspect the printed characters. Character images are original portable PNG specimens. Image choices check immediately.
Select the character shown in both specimens.
Select the image of È (E with a grave accent).
Read the situation, written in English, and the Italian dialogue, then answer in Italian. Some dialogues are read aloud line by line, automatically or with Play dialogue.
You meet your neighbour Anna in the evening.
Anna and Luca are in the kitchen.
Anna and Luca talk after lunch.
Il caffè di Luca è dolce?
Enable Audio Exercises and Text-to-speech to practise every item here. Use the replay control as needed. Listen for meaning as well as for individual words.
Maria compra due mele e un chilo di pane al mercato.
Read the language named in the instruction. QQL supplies the instruction for each direction. Pronunciation is optional; these questions remain available with Audio Exercises off.

rounds.title: Source-language answers, pictures and true or false

prompt.text: These Select exercises answer in the source language or with pictures: Choose the answer (to source), True or false, Listen and choose (to source), Listen and answer (to source), What is in the picture and Listen and pick the image.
Il treno per Roma parte alle nove.

content.text: Type a translation, a missing fragment, a complete word, or a transcription. Accepted answers can include optional wording and alternatives. Accents are preserved; ordinary capitalization, punctuation and spacing are normalized. Only Type the translation and Type the missing word tolerate one omitted or duplicated repeated letter.

prompt.text: Type a natural Italian translation. These examples demonstrate several ways an author can record equivalent answers; the answer notation is never shown as the learner prompt.
The teacher is tired. (The teacher may be a man or a woman.)
Translate the complete sentence. Several natural word orders may be accepted. Keep accents and apostrophes, and check repeated letters when you type.
I am going to Rome tomorrow.
I study at home in the evening.
Today I buy bread and milk.

exercise.hint: Use the contracted definite article before acqua.

prompt.text: Type the missing text. Type the missing word gives the first letter as a hint and still expects the complete word. A phrase with pronunciation audio also accepts its complete spoken form.

exercise.hint: Think of a common household animal.
One barks; you can ride the other.

layout.text: Il David di Michelangelo è a

prompt.text: Enable Audio Exercises and Text-to-speech. For a transcription, type the whole utterance. For missing words, complete the numbered fields in transcript order.
Type the sentence about the train.
Anna tells you when she arrives.
Luca legge un libro in giardino.
Type the translation (to source) takes a source-language translation. Complete the text and Missing letters are typed gaps without and with letters inside words. Name what you see names a picture.

exercise.hint: A drink, then a way to travel.
A way to travel, with its article.

content.text: Build an Italian answer from words, phrases, letters or syllables. Ordinary Arrange consumes each block once; repeated words need repeated blocks. Inline Arrange fills fixed gaps with distinct blocks. Word order and Build the translation allow zero, one or two distractors; Image-prompt ordering allows none.

prompt.text: Tap blocks to build the answer. You can remove a chosen block before checking. Repeated words are separate occurrences.
Put the Italian sentence in order: The cat sleeps.
Put the Italian sentence in order: Anna drinks water.
Put the Italian sentence in order: The train leaves today.
Build: Anna eats bread and Luca eats rice.

correctOrders.text: Anna mangia pane e Luca mangia riso

prompt.text: Build: I go to school by bus.

rounds.title: Pick the words for the gaps

prompt.text: Tap a word for each gap: each word fills one gap and leaves the bank. A word needed twice is offered twice. Gap contents can be removed, moved or swapped.
Complete the sentence about Anna's drink.
Complete the sentences using separate blocks.
Io vado a scuola in autobus.

Translate the English prompt using the available literal blocks. Some questions accept more than one complete translation. Answer-expression notation and typo tolerance do not apply to this exercise type.
I go to school by train.
Anna drinks water and Luca drinks milk.

correctOrders.text: Anna beve acqua e Luca beve latte

prompt.text: Use every available block to write the Italian word for the picture. There are no distractors. Each repeated letter is a separate block.
Build the Italian word for this fruit.
Build the Italian word for this animal.
Build the Italian word for this fruit. Use the singular word.
Build the translation (to source) uses source-language blocks. Put the sentences in order orders lines. Spell what you hear and Spell the word spell a word from tiles without a picture.

correctOrders.text: I go to school by train

correctOrders.text: Anna entra nel bar. Ordina un caffè. Paga e saluta.

correctOrders.text: Buongiorno, un caffè per favore. Subito. Zucchero? No, grazie. Ecco a lei.

exercise.hint: The barista offers sugar before serving.

prompt.text: You drink it when you are thirsty.

content.text: Match each item on the left to its partner. The shuffled columns preserve stable pair identities. Match the pairs can use a variable number of text pairs; Match the words, Match related words and Listen and match use exactly three pairs. Listen and match needs audio enabled.

prompt.text: Match every row before Check. For related words, read whether the task asks for synonyms or opposites.
Match the Italian greeting with its English meaning.
Match each Italian phrase with its English meaning.
Match the English words with their Italian translations.
Match each word with its synonym.
Match each picture on the left with its Italian word.
Match each picture with its word.
Enable Audio Exercises and Text-to-speech. Play each sound and match it to the English meaning. Three sounds have three distinct partners and no distractors.
Listen and match each Italian word with its English meaning.
Match these familiar Italian words to their opposites.
Match each word with its opposite.

content.text: Flashcards present material without a scored answer. Got it completes a card; Review again schedules it again later in this Round. These six cards cover all meaningful combinations of optional pronunciation, usage and usage translation. A usage translation only appears with a usage sentence. Cards with pronunciation audio follow learner Audio Settings.

prompt.text: Read each card. Try Review again once, then Got it when the card returns. These cards can be studied without audio and do not earn correct-answer base XP.
Enable Audio Exercises and Text-to-speech to include these cards. Play the word or the usage sentence, then choose Got it or Review again.
I drink a glass of water.
Picture flashcards show a picture with the word; their audio is optional and never makes them audio exercises. Note cards carry a tip or a grammar note.
Use Lei with people you do not know well; tu is for friends, family and children.
il, lo, la, i, gli, le: the article agrees with the noun in gender and number.

content.text: A Story is a Round played in order: a cover, dialogue lines said by the narrator or by a character, and exercises about them (Build 256 Revision 5). Lines are never skipped: without audio the learner reads them. An exercise marked as needing the Story's audio is skipped, like the listening exercises, when Audio Exercises is off. Only the exercises score. The first Story alternates lines and questions; the second shows the line options one by one and has nothing to score.

prompt.text: Read or listen to the story and answer the questions between the lines. Continue moves on; the scroll log keeps the dialogue.
A cup of coffee on a bar counter
Anna walks into a café in Turin and greets the barista.
Anna walks into a café in Turin and greets the barista.
Put Anna's order in order: A coffee, please.

rounds.title: The same morning, line by line

prompt.text: Each line of this Story shows one option: text after listening, text only, audio only read on request, and audio read aloud although the Story reads on request. Nothing is scored.
A cup of coffee on a bar counter
The same morning, line by line
Anna orders again; every line shows a different option.
Anna orders again; every line shows a different option.

content.text: Assign places items into destinations (Build 256 Revision 7): tap an item, then the group or slot that takes it; Check grades every destination at once. A group may take any number of items, a slot takes one; a reusable item stays in the bank. The presets Sort into groups and Fill the slots author these examples (Revision 7 follow-up). Gaps in a text are authored in the canonical editor; picture regions, grid cells and drag placement wait for a later version.

prompt.text: Sort the words into their groups, or fill each slot with the right word. Tap a word, then its destination; Check when every word is placed.
Sort the words: animals or plants?
Sort the words: animal, plant or object?
Which article goes with each noun?
Which article goes with each noun? An article may serve twice.

content.text: A Page is a card the learner reads and continues (Build 258): headings, paragraphs with bold and italic, quotes, lists, pictures, audio and video links, each with its alignment and a colour from a palette that stays readable in light and dark themes. Nothing is scored. The Page preset authors these examples; a video link opens in the browser.

prompt.text: Read each page and press Continue. The second page has a picture, a Listen button and a video link that opens in your browser.
In Italy a **caffè** is an espresso. People often drink it *standing* at the bar, in a few sips.

**espresso**: a small, strong coffee
**cappuccino**: coffee with foamed milk
**macchiato**: espresso with a drop of milk

Say *buongiorno*.
Order at the counter.
Pay at the till.
Tip: a cappuccino is a morning drink.
A cup of coffee on a bar counter
Careful: *un caffè* is never a large mug of coffee.
Watch how to order a coffee
The video opens in your browser; QuisquisLingo does not play it.
